spec.goal: Allow rsnap to capture its own Settings window on macOS without regressing the existing exclusion of overlay, HUD, loupe, toolbar, and other auxiliary rsnap capture windows.
success_criteria: Starting a capture while the Settings window is open allows the Settings window to appear in the live/frozen capture flow.
rsnap keeps excluding overlay, HUD, loupe, toolbar, and similar auxiliary capture windows from ScreenCaptureKit-based capture paths.
The app-shell to overlay contract exposes a narrow, explicit self-capture exception surface instead of removing the current-process exclusion entirely.
Changing the Settings-window allowlist while overlay worker responses are in flight does not wedge freeze/export flows or strand pending worker responses.
Fresh verification covers the changed Rust crates and the saved plan/runtime state.
constraints: Keep the change scoped to the macOS self-capture behavior for the Settings window.
Do not broadly relax rsnap's self-exclusion policy for auxiliary capture windows.
Preserve the current uncommitted Screen Recording permission-gate work in the primary checkout; do not discard or reset unrelated in-flight edits.
Use repo-native cargo make tasks where an equivalent task exists.

tasks.title: Expose a stable Settings window self-capture identity from the app shell
tasks.objective: Teach the Settings window and app shell to surface a native macOS window identifier that can be used as an explicit self-capture exception.
inputs: Current Settings window creation path in apps/rsnap/src/settings_window.rs
Current app-shell capture startup flow in apps/rsnap/src/app/capture.rs
outputs: A narrow app-shell surface that can provide the Settings window capture identity when present
verification: The Settings window can expose an optional native capture-window identifier on macOS without changing non-macOS behavior.

tasks.title: Parameterize ScreenCaptureKit self-exclusion to allow explicit exception windows
tasks.objective: Replace the hard-coded 'exclude current process with no exceptions' stream filter with an explicit allowlist of self-capture exception windows, and wire the Settings window through that path.
outputs: Overlay/session/backend configuration that can except only the Settings window from the current-process exclusion
verification: The ScreenCaptureKit filter continues excluding the current process by default and only includes windows explicitly provided by the host app.

tasks.title: Harden active-session worker reconfiguration against in-flight response loss
tasks.objective: Preserve outstanding overlay worker responses while Settings-window allowlist changes trigger live-session self-capture reconfiguration.
inputs: Active-session allowlist refresh path in packages/rsnap-overlay/src/overlay.rs
Overlay worker response handling for freeze, hit test, window-list refresh, and PNG export
outputs: A coherent reconfiguration path that updates live streams immediately without dropping in-flight worker responses or wedging active capture state
verification: Automated coverage proves active-session allowlist changes do not replace the worker until pending responses are safely handled.
Automated coverage proves the deferred worker refresh is applied once the matching in-flight response clears.

triggers: Accessing a stable native Settings window identifier requires a broader window-platform abstraction than the current task allows.
Allowing the Settings window through the ScreenCaptureKit filter also unintentionally reintroduces other rsnap auxiliary windows into capture.
Verification shows the self-capture exception must be generalized beyond the Settings window or must change the broader capture architecture.
